claim: The react-router-v6-to-v7-pro codemod automated ~85-90% of migration changes across 461 real-world files with zero false positives.
quote: validated against four real-world repositories spanning 461 total files, the codemod achieved zero false positives and automated approximately 85-90% of all required migration changes

claim: Official upgrade guide; existing APIs still work in library mode for incremental adoption, and React Router has the largest routing ecosystem.
quote: existing APIs still work in library mode, making incremental adoption straightforward

claim: React Router v8 is the 'most boring' major yet; breaking changes are pre-adoptable in v7 behind future flags, so upgrade is flip flags, remove deprecations, bump dep.
quote: React Router's 'most boring' major release yet. Breaking changes are intentionally minimal-all can be implemented in v7 beforehand using future flags

claim: Migrating a standard small SPA from React Router to TanStack Router takes ~2-4 hours and the two routers can coexist during the transition.
quote: The migration typically requires 2-4 hours depending on app complexity... React Router v7 and TanStack Router can coexist during the transition.

claim: React Router is the least-friction default with the biggest ecosystem; TanStack Router wins for TypeScript-first teams needing typed params/search and typed route trees.
quote: TanStack Router's killer feature is 100% type-safe routing, where route params, search params, and loader data are all fully typed without casting.

claim: Adopting the Remix-style data router on a 20-30 route app runs ~3 weeks; community frustration centers on repeatedly broken forwards compatibility.
quote: So many times I've been stung by painful migrations because they don't realise forwards compat is a feature.

claim: Remix was merged into React Router v7 (library-to-framework shift); @remix-run/* packages were renamed @react-router/* and users switch by changing imports.
quote: Remix users able to keep using Remix and switch to React Router v7 when released by just changing the imports.

claim: Switching a medium app between routers is 3-6 weeks depending on reliance on framework-specific features; the routers can coexist and migrate incrementally.
quote: a rough estimate for a medium-sized implementation: 3-6 weeks of engineering time, plus a testing period
